season_overview.title: IIT Bombay Campus Placement Season Masterplan & Recruitment Calendar

months_overview.title: Season Kickoff & Master CV Locking

key_milestones.title: Official Placement Season 2025-26 Kickoff Broadcast
Degree Conversion & Dual Degree Preference Forms
Master CV Verification Portal Opens

months_overview.tactical_guidance: Lock your 1-page (SDE/Quant) and 2-page (Consulting/Core) LaTeX resumes with verified proofs. Any unverified project bullet point will lead to immediate portal debarment.

months_overview.title: Orientation Talks & Masterclasses
months_overview.theme: SARC Core Talks & Cantilever Labs Prep Masterclasses

key_milestones.title: Resume Making Sessions by Cantilever Labs
SARC Alumni Core Talks Kickoff
Finance & Quant Knowledge Sessions
Formal Suit Stalls Reminder & Fittings

months_overview.tactical_guidance: Establish a peer case group for Consulting (3 people) and start daily 2-hour LeetCode medium problem sets for Tech. Complete suit fittings early to avoid late November tailoring rushes.

months_overview.title: Corporate PPTs & Institute Preparatory Tests
months_overview.theme: Top Firm PPTs (Flipkart, Kearney) & Diagnostic Tests

key_milestones.title: Cantilever Labs Consulting Case Masterclass
Institute Preparatory Test (IPT) Set 1 [(DSA+OS+DBMS)]
Institute Preparatory Test (IPT) Set 2 [(DSA+Aptitude+Finance)]
Kearney Pre-Placement Talk (PPT Attendance Mandatory)
Flipkart Corporate Pre-Placement Talk (PPT)

months_overview.tactical_guidance: Treat IPT tests as real Day 1 tests. They give you your true campus rank across 1,600+ candidates. PPT attendance for Kearney, McKinsey, and BCG is strictly tracked for shortlisting eligibility.

months_overview.title: The Online Assessment (OA) Surge
months_overview.theme: Nightly Tests (8 PM - 11 PM), 157 JAFs & Window Collisions

key_milestones.title: Da Vinci Pre-Placement Talk & Quant Test Intro
Kearney JAF Opens (48-hour submission window)
Sony Japan & Squarepoint Capital JAFs Open
Flipkart APM-1 Problem Statement Released (72-hour window)
Google India Pre-Placement Talk & OA Registration
Peak Nightly OA Wave: 2-3 Tests Every Night from 8:00 PM to 11:30 PM

months_overview.tactical_guidance: CRITICAL: Back-to-back 8 PM & 10 PM test fatigue is the #1 reason strong candidates fail OAs. Follow our 15-Minute Brain Wash protocol. Never attempt 24-hr weekend tests on Sunday night after 10 PM due to portal server congestion.

months_overview.title: Peak Shortlist Drops & Slot Matrix Preview
months_overview.theme: Surprise Shortlist Drops, 277 JAFs & D-Day Slotting Finalization

key_milestones.title: First Wave Tech & Quant Test Shortlists Released
IDC Day 1 Companies Roster Announced
Bain & Company & Top Tier-1 Shortlists Drop
Google & Microsoft Interview Rosters Finalized
Official Day 1.1 and Day 1.2 Slotting Matrix Released

months_overview.tactical_guidance: Shortlists drop between midnight and 2:00 AM. Do not panic if your name isn't on Day 1.1 rosters; Day 1.2, Day 2.1, and Day 2.2 hold over 60% of all campus tech and consulting hiring.

months_overview.title: D-Day Interviews (Day 1.1 to Day 15)
months_overview.theme: The 15-Day Battle: Rapid Slots, Selections & Walk-in Rounds

key_milestones.title: Day 1.1 Kickoff: Jane Street, Optiver, Apple, Google, Qualcomm
Day 1.2 Kickoff: McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Goldman Sachs, ITC
Day 2 Sprint: Flipkart, Meesho, Zomato, Micron, NK Securities Walk-ins
Days 3 to 8: Bulk Core Engineering (Tata, Reliance, SLB) & Analytics
Phase 1 Conclusion & Extended Wave Selections

months_overview.tactical_guidance: Stay in interview holding lounges. Keep in close touch with your Department Placement Coordinator (DPC) runner. Over 40 companies issue instant walk-in shortlists when earlier candidates accept offers.

Do keep in mind that this document is part of a larger policy framework. So ensure that you familiarize yourself with it and not limit yourself to just the shared document. 1. Basic Understanding: What is the objective of the Mission and what is the structure of the governing body/committee? What is the budget allocation under the Mission? Which minerals are covered under the Mission and what sectors do these apply to? Deliverable: 1. Prepare a one-page structured brief using the above questions. For the second conversation, please also be prepared with data on the potential for critical mineral (specifically lithium, cobalt and nickel) market in India – global production capacity by geographical concentration, India’s import dependence, growing demand for these in India and globally, etc. The assignment should be submitted in the submission link shared earlier with the title : LohumAssignment_PublicPolicyAnalyst_Name

Students and their runners are requested to check the blog regularly. All students are expected to be familiar with the Skynet platform for the interview schedule. For further understanding, students may visit the link. Credentials for placements would be generated by the end of the day today. The students are expected to carry their own water bottles, A4 loose sheets of paper, working pens, and 30-35 copies of their verified resume. Note that the resumes are strictly for interview rounds and not for walk-ins (Recruiters will directly look at students’ details and verified resumes from the portal). Students should bring the same Verified Resume to the Interviews with which they have filled the JAF. Any Information related to Walk-in applications will be communicated through Placement Blog only. Walk-in applications would be considered primarily via student portal application. Unverified resumes during Interviews will attract a penalty and the concerned recruiter will be informed promptly. The students are required to bring their own laptops (irrespective of Offline/Online mode of Interview), earphones, chargers, mobile hotspots and power banks. Laptops and phones must be fully charged ahead of the interview slot as neither power sockets for charging nor WiFi connections be provided except during the Online Interview of students. calendar_events.title: Placements 2025-26 | Slots and Preferences
calendar_events.snippet: The placement process will begin on December 1st, 2025. Interviews will be held in Hostel-16, A and B wings. Interview slot timings (subject to change on the di...
calendar_events.content: The placement process will begin on December 1st, 2025. Interviews will be held in Hostel-16, A and B wings. Interview slot timings (subject to change on the discretion of the Placement Office) Date Day Slot 1 Slot 2 Dec 1 – Dec 4 Day 1-4 7:00 AM – 3:00 PM 5:00 PM – 1:00 AM Dec 5-Dec 6 Day 5-6 3:00 PM – 11:00 PM – Dec 7 – Dec 15 Day 7-15 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM – For Day 1: Preferences are now open. For Day 2 and onwards: Preferences will be taken before everyday. The window to fill preferences will be 5:00 PM – 7:00 AM of the previous Day for the morning slot & 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM of the same day for the evening slot. Please note that preferences from Day 2 onward have to be filled out separately for each slot. You will see separate preference forms for each slot on the portal. e.g., Preference forms for Day 2.1 needs to be filled from December 1st, 5:00 PM – December 2nd, 7:00 AM, and for Day 2.2 needs to be filled on December 2nd, 7:00 AM – December 2nd, 5:00 PM (before the Slot commences). Results will be announced at the end of each slot, and students will be assigned jobs based on their preferences (explained below). Merged Slots – Day 1: For Day 1, the two slots are considered as merged, which means that a student securing a job in the morning slot will be allowed to interview for a company in the evening slot, only if they have filled a higher preference for a company visiting in the evening slot compared to an offer received in the morning slot. Preferences: Students may get shortlisted for interviews with multiple companies in any given slot. A student may thus get selected by multiple companies, although they can ultimately join only one company. As per standard practice, the Placement Office will collect the students’ preferences for their most preferred job (which is essentially a ranking of the companies, in case the student is offered a job by more than one company). The Placement Office assigns the highest preferred job opportunity that he/she has opted for, while the other companies are requested to offer the lost job to a wait-listed student. All students are required to fill in their preferences using the “My Preferences” in the “Slots and Preference” tab on the student homepage on the placement website. For Day 1, since the slots are merged slots, a combined preference of morning and evening slots will be taken; you will see all the JAFS of the Day 1 companies (will show as Day 1 slot 1). calendar_events.title: Student’s PoC (Runner) Form and Guidelines
calendar_events.snippet: All students appearing for placements are required to mandatorily fill the runner form: https://forms.gle/DJg2CSoX9yB7YgWw6. Runners serve as alternate points o...
calendar_events.content: All students appearing for placements are required to mandatorily fill the runner form: https://forms.gle/DJg2CSoX9yB7YgWw6. Runners serve as alternate points of contact for the placement team to reach out to while a student is busy in an interview. Note: Alumni are not allowed to be listed as runners. Refrain from including their details as a runner, as it will be considered null and void. Only current IITB students can be listed as runners. Guidelines: 1. The placement team gets a status update and conveys urgent/necessary information to the student through runners so that the student is not disturbed during interviews. 2. It’s recommended to have a runner who knows how to use the placement blog and portal so that they can assist with applying for walk-ins and checking out extended shortlists. 3. Make sure they know about your preferences so that they can coordinate better with the placement team, if needed. 4. Runners are strictly forbidden from speaking directly with company officials. Runners are also expected to behave in a calm and professional manner at the venue and maintain a quiet environment. 5. Any misbehavior with other students, company officials, placement team, security team, etc. will invite serious penalties and disciplinary action from the institute (including the runner’s corresponding student). 6. Please note that the shortlisted students and their runners have to compulsorily bring their official ID cards to the venue. Any other student will be made to leave the venue by the security and the student placement team. 7. Interview coordinator (INCs) can not be runner. Deadline: Nov 30, 2025, 11:59 PM.

calendar_events.snippet: A student can earn a maximum of 24 incentive points at the institute level and 10 points at the department level. Preparatory tests will be conducted, through w...
calendar_events.content: A student can earn a maximum of 24 incentive points at the institute level and 10 points at the department level. Preparatory tests will be conducted, through which students can accumulate incentive points. These tests will be organized into 4 sets, with each set comprising 9 tests: 3 Aptitude tests, 3 Coding tests(2DSA+1ML Theory MCQ), 1 Finance and 2 Data analytics tests. Among these 9 tests, students can earn incentive points from a maximum of 3 tests. Although they may attempt any number of tests, incentive points will only be awarded based on the 3 tests from a set. Test Sets 1 2 3 4 Total Institute level tests 3/9 3/9 3/9 3/9 12 Incentive points 3*2 3*2 3*2 3*2 24 The detailed schedule of these tests will be shared shortly on the placement blog. If students miss out on earning points from these tests, they can earn them by attending sessions organized by other institute bodies.

Slot 1 : 3rd August 2025 – 9:30 PM to 11:30 PM Slot 2 : 5th August 2025 – 9:30 PM to 11:30 PM Venue: B. Nag Auditorium, VMCC (Ground Floor). Students are expected to arrive at the venue 15 minutes early. Entry will not be permitted after 9:30 PM. Dress Code: No shorts allowed. IIT Bombay ID card is compulsory for attendance. Each student is expected to attend one Resume-Making Session and one Knowledge Session. Students will be allotted slots on a First-Come, First-Serve (FCFS) basis as per their preference and availability mentioned in the form. Filling out the form is mandatory. This will help us to plan and manage the sessions efficiently. Deadline to fill the form: 6:00 PM, 2nd August 2025. Link to the Form: Here All students are strongly encouraged to attend both sessions to ensure thorough preparation for the placement season.

calendar_events.title: Assessments | Institute Placement Preparatory Activities 2025-26
calendar_events.snippet: The Placement Season in IIT Bombay begins with assessments to help students prepare for resume making, personal interviews, and group discussions. These will be...
calendar_events.content: The Placement Season in IIT Bombay begins with assessments to help students prepare for resume making, personal interviews, and group discussions. These will be conducted by an assessment firm from the first weekend of August. We will have an assessment firm, for the Placement Season to facilitate “Institute Level Student Preparation” (Soft Skills & Interview Prep). It is highly suggested to grab this opportunity to work on your weaknesses/ shortcomings. There would be limited slots available, and considering the strenuous schedule post-semester start, it is strongly advised to follow the time slot that will be allotted to you. What they are offering – Personal Interview (PI): Every student will have to attend an online/offline PI based on the profile preference for 25-30 minutes. This would require students to be dressed formally. Feedback report: An assessment feedback report will be generated personally for every candidate. Modules on GD, PI prep, and sector-specific sessions (non-core) across the months of August. What they are Expecting from the participants – Assessment centres work with clockwork precision. Make sure you are on time. Reporting time will be 15 minutes before your session starts. Seek feedback and ask the panelist for clarification when required. Briefing by Assessment Firm – Professionals from the assessment firm will be briefing the students on how to appear for a personal interview, GD, and how to prepare effective resumes. Fill in your preferences (MANDATORY) – Fill your choice of mock interview profile by August 3, 2025, in the following form, LINK – https://forms.gle/8VjcNeEnDVLMTyS78 It is mandatory to fill out the form to participate in assessments. The form can only be filled out once.

2025-11-30.content: Students are requested to read through the following instructions thoroughly: Students are required to dress professionally and must adhere to Student Placement Policy 2025-26 Students must arrange their own runners who can assist with the entire Interview Process including applying for walk-ins and checking out extended shortlists. Shortlisted students and their runners have to compulsorily bring their official IIT Bombay ID cards to the venue. Any other students will be made to leave the venue by the security and the student placement team. All Information related to Placements will be communicated through Placement Blog only. Students and their runners are requested to check the blog regularly. All students are expected to be familiar with the Skynet platform for the interview schedule. For further understanding, students may visit the link. Credentials for placements would be generated by the end of the day today. Any misbehavior with other students, company officials, placement team, security team, etc. will invite serious penalties and disciplinary action from the institute. The students are expected to carry their own water bottles, A4 loose sheets of paper, working pens, and 30-35 copies of their verified resume. Note that the resumes are strictly for interview rounds and not for walk-ins (Recruiters will directly look at students’ details and verified resumes from the portal). Students should bring the same Verified Resume to the Interviews with which they have filled the JAF. Any Information related to Walk-in applications will be communicated through Placement Blog only. Walk-in applications would be considered primarily via student portal application. Unverified resumes during Interviews will attract a penalty and the concerned recruiter will be informed promptly. The students are required to bring their own laptops (irrespective of Offline/Online mode of Interview), earphones, chargers, mobile hotspots and power banks. Laptops and phones must be fully charged ahead of the interview slot as neither power sockets for charging nor WiFi connections be provided except during the Online Interview of students. A Point of contact has been assigned to each company, and will be assisted by Interview Coordinators. Students may approach them in case of any queries. 2025-11-30.title: Placements 2025-26 | Slots and Preferences
2025-11-30.snippet: The placement process will begin on December 1st, 2025. Interviews will be held in Hostel-16, A and B wings. Interview slot timings (subject to change on the di...
2025-11-30.content: The placement process will begin on December 1st, 2025. Interviews will be held in Hostel-16, A and B wings. Interview slot timings (subject to change on the discretion of the Placement Office) Date Day Slot 1 Slot 2 Dec 1 – Dec 4 Day 1-4 7:00 AM – 3:00 PM 5:00 PM – 1:00 AM Dec 5-Dec 6 Day 5-6 3:00 PM – 11:00 PM – Dec 7 – Dec 15 Day 7-15 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM – For Day 1: Preferences are now open. For Day 2 and onwards: Preferences will be taken before everyday. The window to fill preferences will be 5:00 PM – 7:00 AM of the previous Day for the morning slot & 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM of the same day for the evening slot. Please note that preferences from Day 2 onward have to be filled out separately for each slot. You will see separate preference forms for each slot on the portal. e.g., Preference forms for Day 2.1 needs to be filled from December 1st, 5:00 PM – December 2nd, 7:00 AM, and for Day 2.2 needs to be filled on December 2nd, 7:00 AM – December 2nd, 5:00 PM (before the Slot commences). Results will be announced at the end of each slot, and students will be assigned jobs based on their preferences (explained below). Merged Slots – Day 1: For Day 1, the two slots are considered as merged, which means that a student securing a job in the morning slot will be allowed to interview for a company in the evening slot, only if they have filled a higher preference for a company visiting in the evening slot compared to an offer received in the morning slot. Preferences: Students may get shortlisted for interviews with multiple companies in any given slot. A student may thus get selected by multiple companies, although they can ultimately join only one company. As per standard practice, the Placement Office will collect the students’ preferences for their most preferred job (which is essentially a ranking of the companies, in case the student is offered a job by more than one company). The Placement Office assigns the highest preferred job opportunity that he/she has opted for, while the other companies are requested to offer the lost job to a wait-listed student. All students are required to fill in their preferences using the “My Preferences” in the “Slots and Preference” tab on the student homepage on the placement website. For Day 1, since the slots are merged slots, a combined preference of morning and evening slots will be taken; you will see all the JAFS of the Day 1 companies (will show as Day 1 slot 1). 2025-11-29.title: Student’s PoC (Runner) Form and Guidelines
2025-11-29.snippet: All students appearing for placements are required to mandatorily fill the runner form: https://forms.gle/DJg2CSoX9yB7YgWw6. Runners serve as alternate points o...
2025-11-29.content: All students appearing for placements are required to mandatorily fill the runner form: https://forms.gle/DJg2CSoX9yB7YgWw6. Runners serve as alternate points of contact for the placement team to reach out to while a student is busy in an interview. Note: Alumni are not allowed to be listed as runners. Refrain from including their details as a runner, as it will be considered null and void. Only current IITB students can be listed as runners. Guidelines: 1. The placement team gets a status update and conveys urgent/necessary information to the student through runners so that the student is not disturbed during interviews. 2. It’s recommended to have a runner who knows how to use the placement blog and portal so that they can assist with applying for walk-ins and checking out extended shortlists. 3. Make sure they know about your preferences so that they can coordinate better with the placement team, if needed. 4. Runners are strictly forbidden from speaking directly with company officials. Runners are also expected to behave in a calm and professional manner at the venue and maintain a quiet environment. 5. Any misbehavior with other students, company officials, placement team, security team, etc. will invite serious penalties and disciplinary action from the institute (including the runner’s corresponding student). 6. Please note that the shortlisted students and their runners have to compulsorily bring their official ID cards to the venue. Any other student will be made to leave the venue by the security and the student placement team. 7. Interview coordinator (INCs) can not be runner. Deadline: Nov 30, 2025, 11:59 PM.

2025-09-17.title: Incentive Points Framework
2025-09-17.snippet: A student can earn a maximum of 24 incentive points at the institute level and 10 points at the department level. Preparatory tests will be conducted, through w...
2025-09-17.content: A student can earn a maximum of 24 incentive points at the institute level and 10 points at the department level. Preparatory tests will be conducted, through which students can accumulate incentive points. These tests will be organized into 4 sets, with each set comprising 9 tests: 3 Aptitude tests, 3 Coding tests(2DSA+1ML Theory MCQ), 1 Finance and 2 Data analytics tests. Among these 9 tests, students can earn incentive points from a maximum of 3 tests. Although they may attempt any number of tests, incentive points will only be awarded based on the 3 tests from a set. Test Sets 1 2 3 4 Total Institute level tests 3/9 3/9 3/9 3/9 12 Incentive points 3*2 3*2 3*2 3*2 24 The detailed schedule of these tests will be shared shortly on the placement blog. oa_survival_guide.title: October Online Assessment (OA) Overlap & Fatigue Survival Guide
oa_survival_guide.description: In October, 92 Online Assessments take place across HackerRank, Mercer Mettl, and SHL, alongside 157 JAF deadlines and academic midsem exams. This tactical playbook helps candidates navigate back-to-back testing and mental fatigue.

consecutive_test_strategy.rule: The 15-Minute Brain Wash (Between 8:00 PM and 9:45 PM Tests)
consecutive_test_strategy.action: Never carry disappointment from a missed test case in the 8:00 PM test into the 9:45 PM test. Immediately close your laptop, wash your face with cold water, do 5 minutes of box breathing, and drink cold water with electrolytes. Reset your mental score to zero.

consecutive_test_strategy.rule: Neural Context Switching (SDE Coding → Quant/Analytics Math)
consecutive_test_strategy.action: Switching from writing C++ algorithms to speed mental math requires different brain regions. Before starting a Quant/Analytics test, solve 3 quick mental arithmetic drills (multiplications / Bayes percentages) to activate your numerical intuition.

If you are stuck on problem 3 with 15 minutes remaining, stop attempting an optimal O(N) solution. Implement a clean brute-force O(N²) or O(2^N) solution to capture 30–50% partial points. In campus hiring, partial test cases often differentiate who gets shortlisted.

weekend_window_strategy.window_type: 24-Hour Open Window Assessments (Saturday 12 PM - Sunday 12 PM)
weekend_window_strategy.golden_rule: NEVER take the test between 10:00 PM and 11:59 PM on Sunday.
weekend_window_strategy.why: Historically, over 600 students attempt the test in the final 2 hours. HackerRank and Mettl servers experience severe latency spikes, code execution delays (queue times jump from 2s to 90s), and submission timeout failures.
weekend_window_strategy.best_time_to_start: Saturday 10:30 AM – 1:00 PM or Sunday 2:00 PM – 4:30 PM when mental alertness is high and platform bandwidth is free.

traps_to_avoid: Multi-monitor detection: Disconnect external HDMI cables completely before starting.
Clipboard tracking: Never paste external code. HackerRank logs keystroke cadence and paste volume.
Tab switching: Any window blur of >3 seconds triggers an automated integrity flag to the campus recruiter.
Lighting traps: Ensure bright, uniform frontal lighting. Side shadows trigger 'No Face Detected' or 'Multiple Faces Detected' flags.
Audio sensitivity: Ambient hostel corridor noise or fans can trigger suspicious noise warnings. Test in a quiet room with the door locked.
Eye tracking: Looking away from the screen for >5 seconds generates an alert.
No question backtracking: Once you submit an answer or skip, you CANNOT go back. If stuck, make an educated guess.
No negative marking: Never leave an SHL aptitude question blank before the timer expires.

midsem_fatigue_recovery: Take a mandatory 45-minute power nap between 5:30 PM and 6:30 PM before evening tests.
Selective JAF signing: Do not sign 120 JAFs blindly. An unattempted test after signing a JAF incurs placement cell penalty points. Target 35–50 high-conviction companies.
Keep high-protein snacks (walnuts, almonds, dark chocolate) on your desk. Avoid heavy oily hostel dinners before 8:00 PM.

dday_slotting_playbook.title: D-Day (Dec 1–15) Slotting & Multi-Shortlist Playbook
dday_slotting_playbook.description: How IIT Bombay orchestrates the premier recruiting slots, and how candidates navigate multi-shortlist collisions and walk-in rounds.

slots.prestige: Premier Global HFTs & Tier-1 Tech Titans
slots.characteristics: Highest compensation on campus (₹1 Cr to ₹2.5+ Cr). Fastest round pacing (30–45 mins per technical panel).
slots.collision_strategy: You can physically attend at most 2–3 full interview loops before 3:00 PM. Prioritize the firm where your OA percentile and interviewer rapport was highest.

slots.prestige: Global Management Consultancies, Tier-1 FinTech & Premier Core
slots.characteristics: Premier consulting firms (McKinsey, BCG, Bain) and elite investment banks (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley). Multi-partner case interviews.
slots.collision_strategy: Consulting interviews require rapid mental switching between case rounds and partner fits. If dual-shortlisted with tech/fintech, take the consulting round first as their partner panels have fixed schedules.

slots.timing: December 2: Day (08:00 AM – 04:00 PM) & Night (05:00 PM – 01:00 AM)
slots.prestige: High-Growth Unicorns, E-Commerce Giants & Top Core
slots.characteristics: Massive hiring velocity. Companies issue offers rapidly to prevent candidates from taking Day 3 slots.
slots.collision_strategy: Look for extended shortlists. Day 2 companies often promote waitlisted candidates if Day 1 candidates accept earlier offers.

slots.timing: December 3 – 15: Rolling Daily Slots (12:00 PM – 08:00 PM)
slots.prestige: Core Engineering, Analytics, Enterprise SaaS & PSUs
slots.characteristics: Consistent daily hiring. Core engineering departments (Mech, Civil, Chem, Aero) see their peak selections during this period.
slots.collision_strategy: Keep your stamina high. Selections here are steady and reliable. Never let down your guard during HR and behavioral rounds.

collision_rules.scenario: Shortlisted in two companies in the same slot (e.g. Google and Qualcomm in Day 1.1)
collision_rules.protocol: Notify your Department Placement Coordinator (DPC) at 6:30 AM. The DPC runners will sequence your panels so you complete Round 1 of Company A, then attend Round 1 of Company B while Company A deliberates.

collision_rules.scenario: Receiving an offer while waiting for another interview
collision_rules.protocol: The 1-Offer Rule is absolute: as soon as Company A registers your offer in the placement system, you are placed and automatically withdrawn from Company B.

If Company X has 5 open slots and 3 shortlisted candidates get placed elsewhere in earlier slots, Company X issues an 'Extended Shortlist' on the spot. Candidates on the waitlist are called for instant interviews.

consulting.title: Management Consulting & Strategy
consulting.key_advice: Attendance at Kearney, McKinsey, and BCG PPTs in September is strictly monitored. Buddy rounds run throughout November; practice cases out loud with peers, not by reading casebooks silently.
consulting.timeline_pattern: PPTs in late Sept → JAFs early Oct → Buddy rounds in Nov → Day 1.2 Interviews (Dec 1 night)

sde.title: Software Engineering (SDE)
sde.key_advice: October has 92 OAs. 80% test standard Dynamic Programming, Graph Traversal, and Trees. Master 60-minute timed sprints under HackerRank proctoring conditions.
sde.timeline_pattern: Early JAFs in Sept/Oct → Massive OA surge Oct 10-31 → Shortlists mid-Nov → Day 1.1 & Day 2 Interviews

quant.title: Quantitative Finance & Trading (HFT)
quant.key_advice: Accuracy and speed are everything. Practice 80-question speed math tests (Zetamac). Master Bayes theorem, Markov chains, and expected value puzzles.
quant.timeline_pattern: Da Vinci / Squarepoint PPTs in early Oct → Mettl speed math tests in late Oct → Day 1.1 Interviews (Dec 1, 7 AM)

core.title: Core Engineering & FMCG
core.key_advice: Be ready to draw diagrams and derive equations on paper. Panelists focus on your summer internship and BTP design choices.
core.timeline_pattern: SARC Core Talks in Aug → JAFs in Oct/Nov → Days 3-8 Interviews (Dec 3-8 peak selections)

analytics.title: Product Management, Analytics & AI/ML
analytics.key_advice: Flipkart APM problem statement drops in mid-October with a strict 72-hour turnaround. Expect live SQL tests with window functions.
analytics.timeline_pattern: APM Assignment drops mid-Oct → SQL OAs in Nov → Day 1.2 / Day 2 Interviews

featured_announcements.snippet: The Placement Season in IIT Bombay begins with assessments to help students prepare for resume making, personal interviews, and group discussions. These will be...
featured_announcements.content: The Placement Season in IIT Bombay begins with assessments to help students prepare for resume making, personal interviews, and group discussions. These will be conducted by an assessment firm from the first weekend of August. We will have an assessment firm, for the Placement Season to facilitate “Institute Level Student Preparation” (Soft Skills & Interview Prep). It is highly suggested to grab this opportunity to work on your weaknesses/ shortcomings. There would be limited slots available, and considering the strenuous schedule post-semester start, it is strongly advised to follow the time slot that will be allotted to you. What they are offering – Personal Interview (PI): Every student will have to attend an online/offline PI based on the profile preference for 25-30 minutes. This would require students to be dressed formally. Feedback report: An assessment feedback report will be generated personally for every candidate. Modules on GD, PI prep, and sector-specific sessions (non-core) across the months of August. What they are Expecting from the participants – Assessment centres work with clockwork precision. Make sure you are on time. Reporting time will be 15 minutes before your session starts. Seek feedback and ask the panelist for clarification when required. Briefing by Assessment Firm – Professionals from the assessment firm will be briefing the students on how to appear for a personal interview, GD, and how to prepare effective resumes. Fill in your preferences (MANDATORY) – Fill your choice of mock interview profile by August 3, 2025, in the following form, LINK – https://forms.gle/8VjcNeEnDVLMTyS78 It is mandatory to fill out the form to participate in assessments. The form can only be filled out once.
